text: {"score":2,"justification":"Numbers match the card, and the citations are mostly appropriate. But the summary's conclusion and internal consistency are weak. The leaning of 'high-acuity panel' and the instruction 'Do not pursue recovery' conflict with the evidence and with the hybrid_review output, which was undecided because the 99215 share is far above expected. The text contradicts itself: it calls the panel 'very sick' and says the share is above the expected 14.3%, yet 99215 is 54.7%, 3.8x expected. It also says 'light monitoring' while recommending no pursuit. The sample is small (19 documented 99215 claims). The summary says the 99215 rate for the sickest patients is above peers (65.7% vs 27.5%) and still concludes the case is fine. Several statements are filler or confusing.","problems":["Leaning 'pattern_consistent_with_high_acuity_panel' and 'Do not pursue recovery' are not supported given 54.7% vs 14.3% expected (ratio 3.82, z 8.4) and the tool's 'undecided' result","The documentation 'supports the level billed' claim rests on only 19 documented 99215 claims out of 415, but the summary does not flag the small sample","'The panel is very sick (expected share 14.3%)' is misleading: an expected share of 14.3% implies a modest-acuity panel, and it is inconsistent with the headline","Inconsistent stance: says 'deserves light monitoring' while the next step says do not pursue; the 65.7% vs 27.5% result is dismissed rather than followed up","Cites 'Only 2 of 30 random charts were below billed' alongside '1 of 19', with the figures not reconciled; 5 of 22 notes with data reviewed but no lab on claim is mentioned but not turned into a next step","Does not mention the 4 low-complexity 99215 claims (e.g. C0057861, C0058186) as candidates for record review; the cited examples are all supportive ones","Next steps are not concrete, with no request for more records on the high-share, low-complexity visits"]}
